Permutation groups

Source: R/combinatorics-permgroups.R
PermutationGroup.Rd

PermutationGroup() is the group generated by permutations, given as arguments or as one list, as SymPy's PermutationGroup: generators are resized to a common degree, duplicates (with dups = TRUE) and identities (when there are other generators) are dropped. The group keeps SymPy's caches, so the base and strong generating set computed by the Schreier-Sims algorithm, the state of the product replacement generator and the known properties persist on the object.

Usage

PermutationGroup(..., dups = TRUE, degree = NULL)

group_degree(G)

group_identity(G)

random_pr(G, gen_count = 11, iterations = 50, .random_prec = NULL)

group_base(G)

  base,
  strong_gens,
  pos,
  randomized = FALSE,
  transversals = NULL,
  basic_orbits = NULL,
  strong_gens_distr = NULL
)

basic_transversals(G)

composition_series(G)

Arguments

...

Permutations or one list of permutations.

dups

Remove duplicate generators.

degree

Degree to resize generators of different sizes to.

G, H, K, N

Permutation groups.

gen_count, iterations

Size and warm up of the product replacement state.

.random_prec

Precomputed choices, as SymPy's _random_prec.

base

A base (0 based points).

strong_gens

A strong generating set.

pos

Position of the base points to swap.

randomized

Use the randomized version.

transversals, basic_orbits, strong_gens_distr

Precomputed data.

other

A group, a list of permutations or a permutation.

g

A permutation (or its array form).

factor_index

Return the base images instead of the factors.

original

Express in the original generators.

rank

A rank.

af

Return array forms.

method

"coset" (Schreier-Sims) or "dimino".

strict

Require equal degrees.

p

A prime.

eps

Error bound of the Monte Carlo test.

gr

The group to test normality in.

points

Points of the block or of the stabilizer.

x

A permutation.

t

The variable of the Molien series (default the symbol t).

k

Number of random elements per round.

alpha

A point, or a vector of points for the action on tuples or sets.

action

"tuples", "sets" or "union" for a vector alpha.

beta

A point.

schreier_vector

A Schreier vector of alpha.

pairs

Return (point, permutation) pairs.

incremental

Use the incremental Schreier-Sims algorithm.

n

For make_perm(), the number of generators to multiply, or a vector of generator indices to use in turn.

seed

NULL (the global generator), an integer seed, or a vector of values to use in turn, as SymPy's _randrange.

gens

Generators to use instead of the group's.

slp_dict

Also return the straight line programs of the strong generators.

consec_succ

Number of consecutive successful sifts to stop at.

prop

A predicate on permutations defining the subgroup.

tests

Optional list of level tests.

init_subgroup

A known subgroup of the result.

Value

A PermutationGroup, list, vector, integer or logical.

Details

The functions below are SymPy's methods. Properties: group_generators(), group_degree(), group_identity(), group_order(), group_elements(), is_abelian(), is_cyclic(), is_dihedral(), is_trivial(), is_solvable(), is_nilpotent(), is_perfect_group(), is_polycyclic(), is_symmetric_group(), is_alternating_group(), is_alt_sym(), is_transitive(), is_primitive(), transitivity_degree(), max_div(), is_elementary(). Base and strong generating sets: group_base(), strong_gens(), basic_orbits(), basic_transversals(), basic_stabilizers(), schreier_sims(), schreier_sims_incremental(), schreier_sims_random(), schreier_vector(), baseswap(). Membership and cosets: group_contains(), coset_factor(), coset_rank(), coset_unrank(), coset_transversal(), coset_table(), generator_product(), is_subgroup(), group_index(), subgroup(), group_equals(). Orbits: orbit(), orbits(), orbit_rep(), orbit_transversal(), minimal_block(), minimal_blocks(). Subgroups: stabilizer(), pointwise_stabilizer(), centralizer(), group_center(), normal_closure(), group_commutator(), derived_subgroup(), derived_series(), lower_central_series(), composition_series(), sylow_subgroup(), subgroup_search(), is_normal(), quotient_group(), abelian_invariants(). Elements: generate_dimino(), generate_schreier_sims(), group_generate(), conjugacy_class(), conjugacy_classes(), molien(). Random elements, drawn from the generator that sympy_seed() seeds: random_pr(), random_stab(), group_random(), make_perm().

Examples

G <- DihedralGroup(4)
group_order(G)
#> [1] 8
group_base(SymmetricGroup(4))
#> [1] 0 1 2
orbits(PermutationGroup(Permutation(0, 1), Permutation(2, 3)))
#> [[1]]
#> [1] 0 1
#> 
#> [[2]]
#> [1] 2 3
#>
